lede: The week’s largest diagnosed failure burst was a repaired test-fixture authorization regression. After the VM tests moved to KVM, the first observed VM retry exposed a separate Docker runner reuse bug.

pull_requests.method: Unit is one (PR, head SHA) associated with a devel-base CI workflow created in the window. The devel-only trusted workflow run title supplies the PR number and full SHA when GitHub omits the PR association. Check runs use filter=all, match the three exact required names and join to the sampled head’s PR workflows. A cancelled head is superseded when a newer head for that PR appears in the frame. A first-pass red head recovered only when all required checks had a visible success and the retried red Bazel gate tested the same full synthetic merge SHA. First-pass completeness is limited to visible GitHub records. The workflow collection had 44 CI runs without a unique devel PR association, including other bases.

pr_targets.summary: The 350-head sample yielded 7 distinct targets recovering on 4 heads. Six targets timed out and one Pod target failed with its failed-attempt log unavailable. None of these seven target pairs identifies an intermittent test assertion. The expanded retry review yielded 29 distinct targets with conflicting fresh verdicts on 40 heads, including 5 targets on 5 heads with a logged test assertion failure before the fresh pass. Other pairs include fixture, transport and watchdog failures.
pr_targets.scope: The expanded set contains 67 first-red Bazel heads with another visible Bazel job. 61 had a later invocation on the exact tested SHA. These are retry-selected heads. Match each final FAILED or TIMEOUT target to a later PASSED target on its full synthetic merge SHA and configuration and require remote result events for the same run and shard, excluding cache hits. The unit is a target. Assertion failures identify the phase where the test detected a problem. They leave the cause of the intermittent outcome open. This review does not count Bazel automatic retry cases in otherwise green PR jobs. The full PR population’s intermittent target count is unknown.

mainline.method: Canonical repository, branch devel, command test and BuildBuddy role CI. Paginated invocation search bounded by update time and filtered by creation time locally. Observed creation range 2026-11-13T00:00:45Z through 2026-11-19T23:59:30Z. Each child ID counts once. 845 of 877 children also matched the GitHub push run, attempt and source SHA through the workflow’s deterministic invocation ID.

kvm_cutover.summary: Required VM CI moved to the cluster kvm-vm pool at 05:41 UTC on 20 November. The automatic managed TCG shadow stopped taking work by 07:36 UTC. This follow-up uses devel push attempts after cutover through the 21:11 UTC Actions collection cutoff, outside the seven-day baseline.

mechanism: At 21:06 UTC the failed runner’s receipt recorded a previous successful action and cgroup membership 0::/init. A fixture fingerprint change correctly required the owned K3s baseline to rebuild. The old baseline stopped and the marker was removed before K3s.start called the namespace guard. That guard accepts only 0::/ even though setup itself moves processes into /init and the recycling probe supports both private paths. A healthy, matching baseline returns before this guard, so the warm reuse control does not exercise rebuild.

The failed setup span took 7.86 seconds. Both pytest errors came from the same session-scoped setup. Bazel tried the identical TestRunner action digest on a different worker with a fresh Docker runner and membership 0::/. Both VM scenarios passed. The first runner requested discard. The first failed setup is one fixture incident.

history: The completed 20 November manual comparison ran both VM scenarios in 100 pairs across 89 commits. Managed TCG failed first on 23 pairs and KVM on two. Five managed runs still failed after retry. All KVM runs passed by the final attempt.

Three fresh pairs before routing cutover and one fresh pair after cutover passed on both routes on the first attempt. Shadow admission required a fresh required-route result. Those four devel pairs and the 100 manual pairs retain their original selection and clocks.

merges.summary: Daily GitHub search and PR listing agree on 1,861 merges, of which 1,659 targeted devel. Eleven devel PRs had a completed red required check before merge and 18 had an in-flight check. The other 1,630 had all three checks green in the latest visible rollup by merge time. Nine of the 11 red gates had a VM failure. Exact-head history and timelines were inspected for the 29 candidates. GitHub organization audit records were unavailable, and the visible discussion established no explicit bypass.

findings.title: Make the recycled KVM namespace guard safe to re-enter
findings.frequency: One failure among 13 fresh required KVM target outcomes. The single automatic retry passed.
paragraphs: Make Docker namespace preparation idempotent across initial root entry and the fixture-owned /init cgroup on rebuild. Keep proof of the private cgroup and writable delegated mount, the owned-process cleanup and the discard fence. Arbitrary cgroup membership must still fail closed.

The smallest discriminating check is two fresh actions on one retained runner. First retain a clean baseline, then change one fingerprinted input so the second action enters from /init and must rebuild. Compare against a fresh runner and negative controls for a foreign cgroup and failed cleanup. Require both scenario callbacks and verified cleanup on the repaired path. This candidate has no intervention run yet.

findings.title: Runtime-proxy test identity regression is repaired
findings.frequency: 19 of 63 failed mainline invocations (~30.2%) carry the shared authorization signature.
paragraphs: 2026-11-17T16:27:04Z through 2026-11-18T00:56:50Z by invocation creation. Gateway-budget logs all report PERMISSION_DENIED for the same Runtime-proxy method. Eight other system-test targets co-failed. The grant removal in #17411 left their fixtures borrowing Notifications’ SVID from the same construct as production.

PR #17433 issues a dedicated reader SVID inside the fixture. Production keeps an empty proxy reader list. A fresh gateway-budget execution passed on the candidate and #17433 verified all nine affected targets. Later sampled mainline passes for this target were cached. Keep this incident closed unless the same signature recurs.

findings.title: Managed VM failures explain most red-at-merge cases
findings.frequency: Nine of the 11 devel PRs with a red check at merge had a managed VM failure before the KVM cutover.
paragraphs: Selected failed attempts show a guest shutdown watchdog, a stalled case with a remaining Sandbox or cancellation during the scenario. Some appeared again on workflow retries. Separate the first guest or host fault from cleanup refusing to recycle an unsafe fixture. The earlier native captures distinguished a host QEMU IOTLB assertion and a separate pre-Runtime guest timer/RCU stall.

Required KVM coverage preserves both real VM scenarios. Keep managed restore and teardown evidence in the archive. A remaining managed Firecracker restore error in the post-cutover census occurred on test_parent_delegation. That failure supplied no VM target TestResult. Continue using fresh physical attempts to measure the KVM rollout.

findings.title: Browser readiness repairs and browser watchdogs have different evidence
findings.frequency: BuildBuddy indexes one failed thread-browser run in 74 tracked runs and one failed window-browser run in 76.
paragraphs: The prior projection and navigation fixes retain the cursor and destination-message assertions. The offline window-browser test now waits for its first shape. After those changes, three retry-selected PR heads had a fresh window-browser timeout followed by a fresh pass on the same revision. Their partial logs do not locate the wait or establish a recurrence of the original first-shape issue.

The first fresh natural open-browser stall with readable artifacts can distinguish the Python proxy, Playwright and Chromium. Retain the existing startup profile, proxy phases and failed case trace. A renderer-block control verified capture in the earlier window.

findings.frequency: Five mainline failed invocations each record the Bun extractor and Docker launcher target failures.
paragraphs: PR #17928 repaired the failure cluster after the #17927 red merge. Keep source regressions out of intermittent test counts. The 63 failed test commands also include 12 BUILD_FAILURE exits overall.

continuity.title: VM setup accounting and native profiles
continuity.body: The case deadline begins after shared setup after #17261. VM import profiling is opt-in after #17381. The previous report preserves the native cold-import controls and the compiler, daemon and device time visibility gaps. Current counts do not attribute a reliability change to these patches.

continuity.title: Retained baseline and provider decisions
continuity.body: The earlier census recorded 380 fresh results from 13 November 03:27 through 17 November 07:00 UTC. 225 reasons were unknown. The earlier missing-marker and fingerprint-mismatch boundaries still apply. The seven full post-merge days end at 00:00 UTC on 21 November, after this collection. The KVM result adds a concrete reopen failure on a different retention path.

continuity.title: Prior transport, storage and coverage decisions
continuity.body: The outer BuildBuddy observer incident remains a historical case. The storage-controller exit cause and matched exposure for the old port, TLS, and projection repairs remain open. The prior coverage decisions for unsupported Codex OOM survival and the Debundle memory benchmark are recorded at their original source pins.

limits: The first-pass chart uses a stratified 350-head sample and weights all seven days equally. Exact-head check histories are limited to visible records. The PR retry table overrepresents heads whose owners retried a failed job.

Only 13 fresh KVM VM target verdicts were observed in this short post-cutover census. This gives a diagnosis and an exposure count. A route-wide rate comparison needs matched fresh actions under representative load.

Target result cache hits and unique physical executions answer different questions. The post-cutover KVM table uses explicit result cache fields or complete remote result events. The party that scheduled a shared physical execution can fall outside the invocation sample.

Mainline selection is bounded by the canonical repo, branch, role and update window. The merge audit reconstructs each candidate with visible check records up to its merge timestamp. The historical organization audit trail is unavailable.
The review used existing executions, artifacts and source. No new CI executions or repair experiments were submitted.
